target_title: Verified reproducibility under the deterministic notebook verifier
note: Cross-cutting reproducibility feature (36 owning tasks, 0a-15b plus X1-X4). Per REVIEWER.md, AC-1/AC-2/AC-4 are already proven by scripts/verify_notebook.sh at each task's close: every one of TASK-DL1..36's closing note documents a PASS run (clean top-to-bottom execution, no error outputs, under the 600s cap), confirmed by reading every closing note's PASS line rather than re-running the verifier. AC-4 (no baked cell outputs) independently reconfirmed by parsing the raw ipynb JSON of all 36 committed notebooks directly: zero code cells carry outputs or an execution_count. AC-3 (seeds set before any stochastic operation) is not covered by the deterministic verifier and was checked directly: a static scan of all 36 notebooks finds np.random.seed(...) as the first code cell in every notebook, and (where torch is imported -- all but 0a/1a, which are pure-NumPy theory notebooks with no torch import) torch.manual_seed(...) alongside it in that same first cell; every detected stochastic call (np.random.*, torch.rand*, DataLoader shuffle, nn.Dropout, layer init, train_test_split) occurs in a later cell, so ordering holds in 36/36. This is full-corpus static evidence for a purely mechanical/structural feature, not a pedagogy or derivation-correctness criterion, matching the full-scan approach FEAT-DL1's prior verdict used for its own cross-cutting structural criteria.
